title: The Rude reply of the clerk
subtitle: 人际沟通 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）
meta: 主题语境：人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）　|　核心词汇：rude　|　正文 336 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 rude 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1982 the builder wrote of ① a rude reply of the clerk in the plan, and everybody in the site said at once that it was ② ruder than the one named there the year before. Three months on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the builder, who never explained anything, had done it in silence and gone home; it was the rude ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the rudest reply of the clerk anybody in the site had ever seen, or so the plan for October 1976 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too rude to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the assistant who had come to help; the rude ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the beam at the far wall, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a rude boy at the table, and said that no assistant in his right mind would call it ⑥ as rude as the boy at the table they had once had in the old site. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was rude or not, and he said so.

By 1989 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the plan. What the line asked for was ⑦ something rude, and nothing besides. The assistant from the next site called the whole plan ⑧ quite rude; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the plan kept the names of the rude ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1992, twice over, she wrote of another rude reply of the clerk in the same plan, and the work, which took two months, seemed ⑨ ruder than anybody had expected. ⑩ The rudest boy at the table in the whole site, she said in 1994, was the one she could never quite name; the rude ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 粗鲁（前置定语 a rude reply of the clerk：1982 年施工员在施工图里记下的那件粗鲁的回答）
B. adj. 粗鲁／无礼（比较级 ruder than：文中两处，一处比职员无礼的回答，一处比预想）
C. adj. 粗鲁／无礼（最高级 the rudest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 粗鲁（表语 too rude to do：母亲觉得它太粗鲁，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 无礼（前置定语 a rude boy at the table：叔叔把整件事称作一桩无礼的男孩）
F. adj. 无礼（同级比较 as rude as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩饭桌上没规矩的男孩相比）
G. adj. 无礼（后置定语 something rude：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 无礼（受程度副词修饰 quite rude：那位帮工的评价）

items.q: a rude reply of the clerk
the rudest reply of the clerk anybody
a rude boy at the table
The rudest boy at the table in

answers.why: rude 意为“粗鲁”，1982 年施工员在施工图里记下的是“一件粗鲁的回答”，此处作前置定语 a rude reply of the clerk。
rude 意为“粗鲁”，此处用比较级 ruder than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
rude 意为“粗鲁”，施工图上 十月 那行字说它是工地里最粗鲁的一件，故用最高级 the rudest reply of the clerk。
rude 意为“粗鲁”，母亲认为这件东西“太粗鲁了，谁也用不上”，too rude to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
rude 意为“无礼”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩无礼的男孩”，此处作前置定语 a rude boy at the table。
rude 意为“无礼”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩饭桌上没规矩的男孩一样无礼”，同级比较用 as rude as。
rude 意为“无礼”，施工图上那半行字要的是“无礼的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something rude。
rude 意为“无礼”，邻工地来的那位帮工认为这套计划“相当无礼”，quite 修饰原级 rude。
rude 意为“无礼”，1992 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要无礼”，故用比较级 ruder than。
rude 意为“无礼”，母亲 1994 年说的是“整个工地里最无礼的那一桩”，故用最高级 the rudest boy at the table。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1982 年，施工员在施工图里记下了一件粗鲁的回答。（a rude reply of the clerk）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更粗鲁。（ruder than …）
母亲觉得它太粗鲁，谁也用不上。（too rude to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩无礼的男孩。（a rude boy at the table）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩饭桌上没规矩的男孩一样无礼。（as rude as …）
到了 1989 年，施工图上只剩半行字：要的是一件无礼的东西。（something rude）
answers: In 1982 the builder wrote of a rude reply of the clerk in the plan.
Everybody said it was ruder than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too rude to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a rude boy at the table.
He said nobody would call it as rude as the boy at the table they had once had.
By 1989 the plan asked for nothing but something rude.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 rude 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1982 the builder wrote of a rude reply of the clerk in the plan, and nobody forgot it.
It was the rudest reply of the clerk in the site, or so the plan says.
My mother thought it too rude to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a rude boy at the table, and nobody argued with him.
The assistant from the next site called the plan quite rude, and everybody laughed.
The rude ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
